title: SpaceXAI's Grok Sued For Breaking Ill. Law With Face Scans
source_used: Bloomberg Law (opening paragraphs only, then paywall); Law360 page held only a subscription teaser
key_facts: An Illinois Grok user sued SpaceXAI Corp. and SpaceXAI LLC, owners and developers of the Grok chatbot.
The complaint alleges the companies illegally scanned users' facial geometry when they uploaded photos for editing or analysis.
It was filed Wednesday (7 Oct 2026) in the US District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.
Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act requires written consent before collecting facial geometry data, a public data-retention policy, and no profiting from such data.
Plaintiff Cesar Padilla alleges he uploaded selfies to Grok asking for a professional headshot and a stylised edit.
quote_evidence: An Illinois Grok user sued the AI chatbot’s owners and developers, SpaceXAI Corp. and SpaceXAI LLC, alleging the companies illegally scanned users’ facial geometry when they uploaded photos for editing or analysis.
according to a complaint filed Wednesday in the US District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.
why_it_matters_hint: A lawsuit tests whether uploading a selfie to an AI chatbot counts as handing over biometric data under Illinois law.
notes: Only the opening paragraphs of the Bloomberg Law article were readable; Law360 (the listed outlet) is paywalled. Whether this is a proposed class action is not stated in the text read (Law360's URL path says 'classaction'). SpaceXAI's response is not in the readable text.
